newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - UK equity traders take defensive action.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - UK equity traders take defensive action.

text.p: UK equity options traders took defensive action by either buying puts in the FTSE 100 index or establishing volatility trades as the stock market weakened on Friday, dealers said.
One large deal was to buy 2,000 August 4350 puts at 5p in American style FTSE. In European style FTSE there was a buyer of 2,000 August 4425 puts at 8p.

More complex was a calendar spread which was hedged by selling FTSE futures. The deal was to buy 7,000 August 4725 calls at around 164p and to sell 7,000 September 4725 calls at 220p, making a net credit of 56p per strategy.
The spread was hedged by buying September FTSE futures at 4860.

Changes in market volatility will affect the longer-term September calls more than the August series. If implied volatility increases both options will be worth more but the September calls will have a greater value than the August calls.
The spread will then be worth less than the initial value of 56p and the overall position will make a loss -- provided the futures price remains the same.
Conversely, if implied volatility decreases the spread will widen and the overall position will make a profit.
In reality, directional movement of the futures market will affect the overall profit or loss at a given moment before August expiry.
After the near-term expiry - and if the short calls are still held -- the options will be a straight hedge against September futures.
By the stock market close the cash FTSE index was down 11.4 at 4,851.5 while September futures were down three points at 4,875.
